answer: We formulate a Sybil-resistant protocol where an identity requires a staking collateral bound to a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function. By passing validation through a cryptographic prism, each node commits an opal deposit subject to a subgame-perfect slashing matrix. If an adversary attempts identity multiplication, the opportunity-cost of these bonds escalates quadratically. The expected payoff of an attack converges to a negative value, while the honest strategy remains the unique pearl of our Nash equilibrium.
